summary: This bill amends the Federal Deposit Insurance Act so that custodial deposits (from trusts, plans, or similar) at well-capitalized banks under $10 billion in assets are exempt from brokered-deposit rules up to 20 percent of the bank's total liabilities, with added interest-rate caps when the bank is not well capitalized, and reduces the Federal Reserve's discretionary surplus fund by $4 million in 2036.

scores.thoughts: The bill reduces the Federal Reserve's Discretionary Surplus Fund by $4,000,000 (effective 2036). This is a minor, one-time reduction in funds available to the government/Treasury. The core provisions are regulatory changes for custodial deposits at community banks and have no spending implications. The $4M cut is a negligible budgetary offset, warranting only a very small positive score.
